counterfactual_missing_items: serum tumor markers (CA19-9, CEA, CA125) all negative
no fevers, night sweats, gastrointestinal symptoms
decisive_items: a 15 cm mass possibly arising from the vaginal wall
a hysterectomy for micro-invasive cervical carcinoma in 2002
mesenteric lymph nodes measuring up to 27 mm
response.rationale: R4 directly matches the primary imaging finding of a mass arising from the vaginal wall, supported by the prior cervical carcinoma history. R2 also uses the same spans but labels it as cervical recurrence, which is less directly supported by the raw text. R5 and R1 rely on secondary features (lymph nodes, cecal fistula) that are present but not the most likely diagnosis given the vaginal origin.

rejected.why: Enlarged lymph nodes and LDH are nonspecific; the mass origin and lack of distant metastases argue against lymphoma.
The cecal fistula is a complication, but the mass arises from the vaginal wall, not the gastrointestinal tract.
While the cervical history is relevant, the raw text explicitly states the mass arises from the vaginal wall, making vaginal cancer more direct.
